title: Sequenced customer dependency checker & bridge for private/VPC upgrades
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Enterprise customers requesting Private/VPC/on‑prem deployments frequently fail onboarding due to subtle sequencing issues across firewalls, package upgrades, and dependency ports. Current intake routes only flag 'network not ready' and route to an SRE runbook — that is slow and inconsistent for high-value customers.

Goal: Build a lightweight, customer-run 'sequenced dependency checker' paired with a short-lived 'customer bridge' pattern that (1) identifies the exact sequencing failure (DNS, MTU, port ranges, proxy auth, artifact pull), (2) provides prescriptive remediation steps, and (3) offers an optional temporary bridge mode that proxies limited traffic to let onboarding proceed while longer upgrades are scheduled. The outcome should reduce handoff tickets, shorten time-to-validate, and improve predictability for Private deployments.

Scope: MVP covers Linux-based on‑prem installs + VPC peering (no Windows agent in MVP). Focus on network checks (TCP/UDP, MTU, DNS), artifact fetch validation (S3/GCS/ecr), and a bridge workflow that supports customer opt-in with RBAC audit logs. Work includes PM spec, small Console UI for 'Run preflight' and 'Enable bridge', eng backlog items, and a customer-facing KB article.
acceptance_criteria: A hosted UI flow in Console that allows designated customer admins to run the sequenced checker and view step-by-step failures and remediation guidance
Checker reproduces the most common failure classes we see in onboarding tickets (DNS resolution failure, blocked egress ports, MTU-related large-packet drops, artifact fetch permission errors)
Optional bridge mode can be enabled by customer admin in Console for up to 72 hours; enabling creates an auditable temporary tunnel with limited scope and automatic expiration
Back-end telemetry surfaces the top 5 failing checks with aggregated counts in the onboarding dashboard
KB article and one-pager remediation checklist drafted and reviewed by Solutions Engineering
Security review completed and bridge flow approved by Security and Compliance teams
updates: 2025-01-15: Ticket created after recurring onboarding incidents (Customer Success triage). Initial scoping call with Solutions Eng and SRE attended by Aisha, Marcus, and Priya Nair.
2025-01-22: Decision to limit MVP to Linux agent + VPC peering. Windows support to be tracked as follow-up (PM-211408 planned).
2025-02-05: UX sketch approved in principle — Console will add 'Preflight checks' card to Private Deployments landing page. Design to deliver final screens by 2025-02-18.

2025-02-12: Engineering spike (ENG-14822) completed — prototype checker successfully validates DNS and port connectivity in lab cluster. Performance: checks complete within 18s on average for standard test vectors.

2025-02-20: Security flagged two items for bridge design: (1) ensure bridge keys are customer-specific, stored in KMS with short TTL; (2) audit log must capture who enabled/disables bridge. Action: add security acceptance criteria and a review checkpoint (security_review_required=true).
2025-02-27: Draft KB and PRD uploaded. Linked PR for prototype agent: https://github.com/redwood-inference/proto-agent/pull/219
2025-03-01: Cross-functional kickoff scheduled for 2025-03-04. Eng planning to split work into three tickets: agent checks, bridge orchestration, console UI.
risk_and_mitigation: Risk: Bridge surface increases attack surface and could be misused to bypass customer policies. Mitigation: limit bridge scope by default (only egress for artifact pulls and control-plane API), enforce customer admin approval, short TTL credentials, HSM/KMS backstop, and mandatory audit logging. If Security blocks any bridge instrumentation, fallback is to publish more prescriptive remediation playbooks and expand Solutions Eng runway.
notes_for_engineering: Champion for ENG: Marcus Lee. Proposed tech approach: lightweight agent run via customer-run script or short-lived container that calls back to Redwood preflight service over TLS with pinned certs. Use existing KV cache to store recent check results for 24h. Bridge uses our edge relay with restricted ACLs. See ENG-14822 for spike artifacts.
customer_stories: Large enterprise (FinTech) failed onboarding due to MTU 9000 mismatch when peered over partner transit; resolution required packet-capture and replay over multiple windows, delaying launch 3 weeks
SaaS customer had artifact fetch blocked by a corporate egress proxy requiring custom CA — preflight should have highlighted TLS trust failure and suggested CA install steps
